# Checked for you

These 119 rules apply now, and tooling or an AI review checks them, so you don't need to read them in advance. A failed check names its rule; look it up here.

## Enforced by tooling (60)

### Data and sync (DATA)

**DATA-01** · MUST · Every feature works offline; the network only adds sync and sharing.\
*Verified by:* CI: test suite passes with the network disabled

**DATA-02** · MUST · File formats and schemas carry a version, and every version change ships an automatic, tested migration. Migration tests use real sample files from every released format version. A storage-model change ships an export path back to the previous open format, so no migration strands users.\
*Verified by:* CI: migration tests over the sample-file corpus, one file set per released format version

**DATA-03** · MUST · Writes are crash-safe (atomic replace or journaling): a crash never corrupts saved data.\
*Verified by:* CI: crash-injection test on the write path

### Security (SEC)

**SEC-01** · MUST · `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide (`unsafe_code = "deny"` in the workspace lints). A crate that needs it has an ADR and a crate-root `#![expect(unsafe_code, reason = "DR-NNNN")]` that CI checks. Every `unsafe` block has a SAFETY comment, is judged sound by the independent AI review (CI-03) against the Rust Reference and t-opsem decisions, and runs under Miri (SEC-19). Permit: `unsafe` in FFI crates under the same conditions, with the permit cited in the `expect` reason.\
*Verified by:* CI: workspace lint table (QA-01) with `undocumented_unsafe_blocks`; `expect` reason resolved to an ADR; Miri job; AI review: soundness of each `unsafe` block

**SEC-02** · MUST · cargo-deny checks every pull request for advisories, licenses and duplicate dependencies, and a daily scheduled scan covers the default branch and every supported release tag (REL-09). A written policy names the advisory severities that block merges and releases. Each deny.toml suppression has a justification and an expiry date. From 1.0, advisories that do not affect the suite get a VEX statement. Clippy's security lints (QA-01) are the project's static analysis, under the same threshold.\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-deny pull-request job and daily scheduled job; suppressions without an expiry fail

**SEC-03** · MUST · No secret enters the repository. A secret scanner the organization runs itself (Betterleaks or an equivalent) checks every push in CI and in a pre-commit hook. A leaked secret is revoked before it is removed from history.\
*Verified by:* CI: secret-scanner job on every push, on each pull request's title and description, and daily; pre-commit and commit-msg hooks

**SEC-20** · SHOULD · A dependency-update bot runs weekly for Cargo and monthly for CI actions and toolchains, groups related crates, and waits at least 7 days after an upstream release except for security fixes. Cargo's native minimum publish age goes into the template once it reaches stable Rust.\
*Verified by:* CI: bot configuration in the template; weekly Cargo and monthly action and toolchain update pull requests

### Privacy (PRIV)

**PRIV-07** · MUST · Each app keeps a machine-readable data manifest of every endpoint and data flow: data sent, purpose, sensitivity category, default state, retention and review link (PRIV-08). CI fails when code, or an integration test run in a network sandbox, contacts an undeclared host; this gate applies from first release.\
*Verified by:* CI: manifest schema check; network-sandbox integration test fails on an undeclared host

**PRIV-09** · MUST · An app includes no third-party analytics, advertising, attribution, tracking or crash-reporting SDK. Permit, by ADR: an open-source client for a self-hostable, organization-run endpoint, sending only after the user's PRIV-04 approval.\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-deny ban list

### Accessibility (A11Y)

**A11Y-03** · MUST · Color never carries meaning alone. Design tokens pass WCAG contrast of 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for large text and non-text UI, focus indicators included, checked in the light, dark and high-contrast themes for every registered accent hue (BRAND-01, BRAND-05).\
*Verified by:* CI: contrast test over tokens, per theme and hue

### Internationalization (I18N)

**I18N-03** · MUST · CI runs a pseudo-localized build to catch hard-coded strings and truncation, expanding strings by 50% (I18N-11).\
*Verified by:* CI: pseudo-locale build and screenshot check

**I18N-11** · SHOULD · Sentences are never built from fragments or across several controls. Layouts tolerate text 50% longer than English. Access keys are translated together with their labels.\
*Verified by:* CI: no clipped text in the pseudo-locale screenshots at 50% expansion; Review checklist: no concatenated strings

### Interface (UX)

**UX-01** · MUST · Visual style comes only from the shared design tokens, in the DTCG 2025.10 format; no hard-coded colors, sizes or fonts.\
*Verified by:* CI: lint for hard-coded colors, sizes and fonts

**UX-15** · MUST · UI text follows the suite writing guide: one English variant; one capitalization style per element type, chosen as a class-2 decision; verb-first labels naming the action and its object; no OK, Yes or No buttons; an ellipsis only on commands that need more input before acting, as defined by the same decision; toggles named by their positive state, without Enable or Use; typographic quotes and dashes; no internal names; errors without blame or jokes, next to the problem, with a fix action where possible. A CI lint over the `.ftl` source strings checks what it can. Details: interface guidelines.\
*Verified by:* CI: `.ftl` string lint; Review checklist: writing guide

### Brand (BRAND)

**BRAND-01** · MUST · Each app has one registered accent hue (BRAND-05). Lightness and chroma are fixed suite-wide for each accent role (text, fill, focus ring) in each theme (light, dark, increased contrast). A class-2 decision chooses one of: (a) the muted chroma every hue can share in sRGB; (b) fixed lightness with each hue at its own maximum chroma up to a cap; (c) accents defined in Display P3 with gamut mapping to sRGB as fallback. Starting points: L ≈ 0.50–0.55 for fills and text in the light theme and L ≈ 0.65–0.75 for accent text in the dark theme; yellows and oranges are shown rendered in the demo evidence, not only computed. The AppStream light and dark brand colors (PLAT-11) are generated from these tokens.\
*Verified by:* CI: contrast test over tokens per hue, role and theme; accent choice recorded in the interface guidelines

**BRAND-03** · MUST · Every crate published to crates.io is named `kreqo-` followed by one plain word, such as `kreqo-sync`; crates that are never published are exempt. Names are reserved on crates.io as soon as there is code to publish.\
*Verified by:* CI: crate-name check over the workspace's publishable crates

### Performance (PERF)

**PERF-02** · MUST · An idle app uses no CPU: rendering and work are event-driven.\
*Verified by:* CI: idle CPU sample at zero

### Platforms, distribution and updates (PLAT)

**PLAT-01** · MUST · Platforms are tiered: Tier 1 is tested in CI and blocks releases, Tier 2 is built in CI, Tier 3 is best-effort.\
*Verified by:* CI: Tier 1 matrix as required checks

**PLAT-04** · SHOULD · Each repository ships a Nix flake with a development shell and a package for each app and tool it holds; Nix stays optional, and cargo alone builds every project.\
*Verified by:* CI: `nix flake check` and `cargo build` without Nix

### Code quality and testing (QA)

**QA-01** · MUST · Code is formatted with rustfmt and passes Clippy; warnings fail CI. Every crate inherits one lint table: crates in the root workspace through `[lints] workspace = true`, and a nested workspace or a repository outside the monorepo through a generated copy of the root's table, an outside repository's taken from the conventions version it names. CI checks the inheritance and each copy. Suppressions use `#[expect(lint, reason = "…")]`; an `allow` attribute, inner or outer, fails CI. The table enforces SEC-01: `unsafe_code`, `undocumented_unsafe_blocks` and `missing_safety_doc`. Parser, importer and sync crates, which their project's `project.toml` lists, add QA-02's `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic` and `indexing_slicing` as crate-level attributes, and crates whose `publish` isn't `false` deny Clippy's `pedantic` group the same way; CI checks both. Bans for every crate use `disallowed-methods` in the root `clippy.toml`, each with a reason; any other `clippy.toml` repeats them, which CI checks.\
*Verified by:* CI: rustfmt; Clippy with `allow_attributes` and `allow_attributes_without_reason`; an `allow` grep, which also catches the inner attributes Clippy skips; checks that every crate inherits the workspace lints, that each copy matches the root's table, that listed crates and crates whose `publish` isn't `false` carry their attributes, and that every `clippy.toml` repeats the root's bans

**QA-03** · MUST · Core logic has unit and integration tests; invariants such as merges, scheduling and migrations have property-based tests.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo test` and proptest targets

**QA-07** · MUST · Coverage is reported on every pull request. Crates whose `publish` isn't `false` keep at least 80% line coverage, and no pull request lowers their coverage.\
*Verified by:* CI: coverage report, threshold and comparison with the base branch

**QA-08** · MUST · Mutation testing (cargo-mutants) covers `xtask`, which runs the checks, and every crate whose `publish` isn't `false`. A pull request that changes them runs `cargo mutants --in-diff`, and a mutant that survives in the diff fails it. A full run on a schedule files the mutants that survive as issues.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo mutants --in-diff` on pull requests; scheduled full run that files issues

**QA-14** · MUST · Repositories contain no generated executables or unreviewable binaries. Binary assets such as fonts, images and test fixtures follow LEGAL-14.\
*Verified by:* CI: binary-file check against the LEGAL-14 directory

**QA-15** · SHOULD · CI fails on unused dependencies (cargo-shear or the `unused_crate_dependencies` lint).\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-shear

**QA-16** · SHOULD · TODO comments reference an issue (`TODO(#123)`), so deferred work stays tracked.\
*Verified by:* CI: TODO lint

### Documentation (DOC)

**DOC-01** · MUST · Every repository has README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, CHANGELOG, LICENSE and CODE\_OF\_CONDUCT files, from the template.\
*Verified by:* CI: required-files check

**DOC-02** · MUST · Public crates set `#![deny(missing_docs)]`. Runnable examples live in the crate's `examples/` folder where they help; a doc example on every item is not required.\
*Verified by:* CI: `missing_docs` lint

**DOC-03** · MUST · Doc tests and the `examples/` directory compile and run in CI.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo test --doc` and `--examples`

**DOC-06** · MUST · An ADR that deviates from a rule declares `deviates: [RULE-ID@version]`, its scope (crates or paths), the reason, the risk and mitigation, and a review-by date. CI lists active deviations and fails when a review date has passed.\
*Verified by:* CI: deviation lister and review-date check

**DOC-11** · MUST · Each published crate's README states its status (stable, experimental, internal, deprecated, placeholder) and maintenance commitment, and is generated from crate-level docs (cargo-rdme), with CI failing on drift. Every published crate package contains its license texts.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo rdme --check`; license files in the package

**DOC-15** · SHOULD · docs.rs builds every crate with all features and shows feature gates; each Cargo feature is documented in the crate docs and in Cargo.toml.\
*Verified by:* CI: `cargo doc --all-features` with `doc_cfg`

### Versioning and releases (REL)

**REL-01** · MUST · Every public interface follows Semantic Versioning: crate APIs, CLI flags, file formats, the sync protocol, the plugin API, design tokens (names and meanings) and component APIs. *Breaking* for crate APIs follows the [Cargo SemVer chapter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/semver.html); the PR states, as an assumption, whether a possibly-breaking change is treated as breaking, and the release summary names it. Token diffs appear in the changelog. Apps also follow a time-based cadence (REL-10).\
*Verified by:* cargo-semver-checks; token diff job; Review checklist: possibly-breaking changes stated in the PR

**REL-02** · MUST · cargo-semver-checks runs on every pull request that changes a crate whose `publish` isn't `false`, against its last published version once it has one.\
*Verified by:* CI: cargo-semver-checks against the last published version

**REL-03** · MUST · Pull-request titles follow Conventional Commits, and CI lints them. Titles describe the change as users would see it, fixes reference their issue, and performance claims cite measurements. Changelogs are generated in the Keep a Changelog format.\
*Verified by:* CI: pull-request title lint; git-cliff

**REL-04** · MUST · Each crate declares its MSRV, which follows a stated window (for example latest stable minus two). Workspaces use resolver 3. An MSRV job checks publishable crates with the committed lockfile, and each changelog release section states its MSRV. Raising the MSRV is a minor version bump.\
*Verified by:* MSRV job with `--locked`

**REL-14** · MUST · A PR that breaks a public interface adds a migration-guide fragment: what changed, why, how to migrate, a before/after example and searchable names. A PR with a user-visible feature adds a release-note fragment. CI validates fragments, and a deprecation attribute never replaces one.\
*Verified by:* Fragment validation job

### Repository and CI (CI)

**CI-01** · MUST · The default branch is protected: no direct pushes, changes land through pull requests, and force-pushing to or deleting protected branches and release tags is blocked. History is rewritten only through a documented expunging process; each use is a class-3 decision, and once there are two maintainers, both approve it. New collaborators start with read access.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: branch and tag protection; default collaborator role

**CI-02** · MUST · Every pull request passes all required checks before merge, and a missing check counts as a failed one. Every project's required checks include format, lint, tests, docs, cargo-deny and the AI review (CI-03). Crates whose `publish` isn't `false` add semver (REL-02), coverage (QA-07), mutation testing of the diff (QA-08), replay of each fuzz target's corpus, the MSRV build (REL-04) and the feature powerset (CI-17); `xtask` adds mutation testing of the diff (QA-08).\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: required checks list; CI: an aggregate job fails when a required job is missing or failed

**CI-03** · MUST · Every change is reviewed before it merges by a reviewer other than its author: the independent AI review, a reviewer agent that runs in its own job with a fresh context and no write access to the code, never sees the session that wrote the change, and checks it against the written review rubric. Its verdict is a required check (CI-02), and an unreadable verdict fails it. The founder's hand-written changes get the same AI review. Gated changes also follow CI-15.\
*Verified by:* CI: the AI review's verdict is a required check, and a missing or unreadable verdict fails it

**CI-04** · MUST · Tier 1 platforms build and test on every pull request; Tier 2 platforms build nightly.\
*Verified by:* Platform matrix job

**CI-05** · MUST · CI workflows come from one source, the conventions in the monorepo, which runs them directly. A repository outside the monorepo takes them at a pinned conventions version, and a drift check fails when its copy differs from that version.\
*Verified by:* CI: drift check in each repository outside the monorepo

**CI-06** · SHOULD · A pull request merges automatically through a merge queue once it passes every required check (CI-02) and has any approval CI-15 requires, so the default branch is always green. A `hold` label pauses one pull request's merge until it is removed. Where the forge offers no merge queue, a pull request merges only when its branch is up to date with the default branch.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: auto-merge on; merge queue enabled, or up-to-date branches required

**CI-07** · MUST · Workflow steps reference actions by their repository and full commit SHA, with the version as a comment, and container images by digest.\
*Verified by:* Pin check in the workflow analyzer (CI-09)

**CI-08** · MUST · Every workflow runs with the least privilege it needs: read-only or no permissions by default, writes granted per job, and checkouts never persist credentials. Where the forge lacks per-workflow permissions, the same outcome is enforced through repository settings and scoped tokens.\
*Verified by:* Workflow analyzer: permissions block; credentials not persisted

**CI-09** · MUST · Workflows never run untrusted PR code with secrets or write tokens: no privileged-trigger checkout of the PR head. Pull-request workflows hold no secret beyond the AI model key and the agent identity's key. Code that a maintainer or the agent identity pushed to the repository's own branches isn't untrusted, so agent jobs may run it with the agent identity's token, while the AI review reads a pull request without running the code or hooks it carries. Untrusted event data (titles, branch names, commit messages) reaches scripts only through environment variables. CI configuration is linted by a workflow analyzer (zizmor where it covers the forge's syntax).\
*Verified by:* zizmor or an equivalent workflow analyzer; Settings audit: the secrets pull-request workflows can read

**CI-10** · MUST · Runners for PR or untrusted code are ephemeral and isolated in a container or VM: no host runners, no privileged containers, no host networking or Docker socket, no access to internal services. Workflows on pull requests from outside contributors need a maintainer's approval to run; those that the agent identity or the dependency-update bot (SEC-20) opens don't. Release jobs run on separate dedicated runners that never run PR code.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: runner labels and isolation; approval for outside workflows

**CI-12** · MUST · Every PR uses the PR template: the intent or issue it implements, and its ADR when it has one; a plain-language summary; each acceptance criterion with the tests that check it; the assumptions made, each with its class under the dilemma protocol and its reason; the demo evidence, which CI fills in, with before/after screenshots or a recording for UI changes; new dependencies, each with why it is needed and its license; docs updated or not needed; risks, compatibility impact and rollback; and the AI disclosure that GOV-03 requires. CI checks that the sections are filled in. Details: the PR template.\
*Verified by:* PR template section check

**CI-13** · MUST · Each PR covers one topic: refactors and cleanups never mix with behavior changes. PRs are squash-merged only, with the forge's squash message set to the PR title as subject and the PR description as body, so branch commits stay scaffolding and every commit on the default branch builds and passes CI.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: squash merge is the only merge method, with the title-and-description message; Review checklist: single topic

**CI-15** · MUST · A CODEOWNERS file, generated from a single list of paths, makes the founder the code owner of every path whose change is a gated change, and of `docs/decisions/`. A pull request that changes such a path merges only with the founder's approval of its latest commit and a linked ADR; no other pull request needs a human approval.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: code-owner review required and stale approvals dismissed; CI: a pull request that changes a code-owned path fails without a linked ADR or without the founder's approval of its latest commit

**CI-16** · MUST · CI and release builds use a pinned Rust toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml`), bumped by deliberate PRs that fix new lints. Every workspace commits `Cargo.lock`, and CI, release and install instructions use `--locked`.\
*Verified by:* `--locked` in workflows; toolchain file present

**CI-17** · MUST · Each package builds and passes Clippy for every feature on its own and with no default features (`cargo hack --each-feature`) on every PR. Crates whose `publish` isn't `false` also pass `--feature-powerset --depth 2` on every PR, and other packages run it on a schedule. Crates targeting the web also get a wasm32 check on every PR.\
*Verified by:* cargo-hack job; wasm32 check job

**CI-18** · MUST · AI reviews run from a separate, clearly labeled bot identity and name the model that ran them. A blocking finding from the independent AI review (CI-03) holds the merge until a fix passes a new review; after three failed fix attempts, the pull request is marked blocked and listed in the digest. A question that the AI review escalates to the founder holds the merge until it is settled under REV-04.\
*Verified by:* Settings audit: bot identity labeled; CI: the merge waits for an approving verdict

**CI-19** · SHOULD · CI runs a spell checker (typos) with a project dictionary and one English variant, skipping translations; Taplo for TOML formatting; markdownlint; and freshness checks on generated feature and example indexes.\
*Verified by:* typos, Taplo, markdownlint and freshness jobs

### Governance and contribution (GOV)

**GOV-07** · MUST · GOVERNANCE.md states the decision model (GOV-09); who holds each decision right (starting work on intents, accepting decision pull requests and gated changes, overriding class-2 decisions, releases, merges per area); who holds each sensitive access (forge admin, the agent identity and its keys, CI secrets including AI model keys, signing keys, registry ownership, DNS); how people join and leave each role; and the escalation path (REV-04). Names live only in GOVERNANCE.md, in ADRs and in files that tooling reads, such as CODEOWNERS; other documents link to GOVERNANCE.md.\
*Verified by:* CI: GOVERNANCE.md present with required sections

**GOV-16** · MUST · Only humans appear in the git author field, and only humans or the forge's merge identity in the committer field. AI tools appear in commits only in the `Co-Authored-By` disclosure trailer (GOV-03), and on the forge only through the agent identity, which the founder answers for, or as the independent AI review (CI-03). CI rejects commits that break this.\
*Verified by:* CI: author and committer fields checked against the contributor list and the forge identity

### Licensing and compliance (LEGAL)

**LEGAL-01** · MUST · Licenses follow three groups. An app's own crates (its core and UI shell) are GPL-3.0-or-later; servers and hosted services are AGPL-3.0-or-later; file formats, protocols, algorithms, shared libraries, tools, and the plugin interface and SDK are MIT OR Apache-2.0. Before the first outside contribution, the GPL and AGPL texts carry additional permissions under their section 7, drafted with legal counsel: distribution through app stores whose terms add restrictions, linking the UI toolkit under its non-GPL license, and combining an app with OSI-licensed plugins that use only the published plugin interface (EXT-05). Any other license needs an ADR.\
*Verified by:* CI: each crate's license field matches its group; Review checklist: group of a new crate

**LEGAL-02** · MUST · Every file carries an SPDX license header, following the REUSE specification.\
*Verified by:* `reuse lint`

**LEGAL-03** · MUST · Dependency licenses are compatible with the project's license, enforced by cargo-deny. Dependencies of MIT OR Apache-2.0 crates use only MIT, MIT-0, Apache-2.0, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, CC0-1.0, BSL-1.0, Unicode-3.0 or Unicode-DFS-2016; any other license, MPL-2.0 included, needs an ADR for that dependency.\
*Verified by:* cargo-deny `licenses` against the list

### Lifecycle and continuity (LIFE)

**LIFE-01** · MUST · Every project declares its stage (incubating, in review, stable, unmaintained, archived) in its `project.toml` and in its README. Only stable projects publish stable-channel releases or carry the Kreqo name. Any stage can move to unmaintained, and an unmaintained project returns to incubating when someone takes it on.\
*Verified by:* CI: stage in each `project.toml` present and valid; README badge generated from it

## Checked by AI review (59)

### Architecture (ARCH)

**ARCH-01** · MUST · All logic is written in Rust. Other languages appear only where a platform, format or tool requires them (shaders, markup and styles, translations, design tokens, interface definitions, CI and packaging files, mobile glue) and never hold business logic.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no business logic outside Rust

**ARCH-02** · MUST · Domain logic lives in UI-independent crates; UI crates contain presentation only.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: core crates have no UI dependency; UI crates hold no domain logic

**ARCH-04** · MUST · Each concept (type, rule, constant) is defined once and imported everywhere else.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no duplicated type, rule or constant

**ARCH-05** · MUST · New capabilities follow the dependency ladder: a maintained, vetted, license-compatible crate; else a contribution to a close one; else a focused crate of our own; else a mature C library behind a safe Rust API. A C library, and a focused crate that starts a new project, need an ADR. A contribution to a close crate is a human-only step (GOV-04); until it lands, a focused crate of our own may stand in.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: ladder step named in the pull request; ADR linked for a C library or a crate that starts a new project

**ARCH-06** · MUST · Project scripts and build tasks are written in Rust (cargo xtask), not shell. CI workflow files, packaging manifests and Nix flakes (PLAT-04) are outside this rule and follow ARCH-01.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new automation lives in the xtask crate

**ARCH-07** · SHOULD · Shared code moves into its own crate on its third use, not before. UI patterns follow UX-02 instead.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: extraction justified by three call sites, or by UX-02 for a UI pattern

**ARCH-08** · SHOULD · Crates are small and single-purpose, with optional functionality behind Cargo features.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: one purpose per crate; optional code behind a feature

**ARCH-09** · SHOULD · Configuration, UI descriptions and content specs are declarative where the domain allows.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new config or spec is data, not code

**ARCH-10** · SHOULD · Declarative specs compile to their output ahead of time. Runtime code generation needs an ADR and never ships on iOS.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: ADR linked for any runtime code generation; iOS build excludes it

**ARCH-15** · SHOULD · Code stays plain enough to review in a web diff. A new proc-macro, or new heavy generic or trait machinery, is justified in its pull request, and async in a core crate needs an ADR. Changes match the surrounding style and never add a second way to do what the codebase already does one way.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new macro or generic machinery justified in the pull request; ADR linked for core async; one way per thing

**ARCH-17** · SHOULD · Code promoted into a shared crate first meets the library bar: docs (DOC-02), tests, the workspace lints, a compatible license, and minimal `unsafe` and dependencies.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: library bar items ticked on the promotion PR

### Data and sync (DATA)

**DATA-04** · SHOULD · Existing open formats (CommonMark, iCalendar) are preferred over new ones; any new format gets a written specification.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: format choice justified; specification linked for any new format

**DATA-05** · SHOULD · CRDTs are used where concurrent edits have to merge, such as shared text; simpler append-only logs where they suffice.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: merge strategy stated per data type

**DATA-11** · MUST · User content, and the records an app keeps of the user's work and the parameters it fits to them, such as review logs and scheduler parameters, live in documented open files that other tools can read. Any database or index is a cache that can be rebuilt from those files.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: every data type has a file representation; rebuild-from-files test present

### Security (SEC)

**SEC-05** · MUST · Projects meet OSPS Baseline v2026.08.28, re-pinned deliberately on each Baseline release: Level 1 from the first commit, Level 2 by first release, Level 3 by 1.0. Evidence is published through the Best Practices badge's Baseline levels or a Security Insights file. The practices behind Scorecard's checks are enforced by forge-neutral tools (CI-07 to CI-10, QA-14, SEC-20); a Scorecard score is not a target.\
*Verified by:* Release checklist: Baseline level evidence (badge or Security Insights file)

**SEC-11** · MUST · Cryptography uses only published standard algorithms and protocols from vetted, maintained crates chosen by ADR; no primitive or protocol is invented or modified. Keys and nonces come from a CSPRNG. TLS goes through rustls, version 1.2 or later, with certificate verification always on. Algorithms are swappable by protocol version.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: cryptographic crates match the ADR; no custom primitives; rustls with verification on

### Privacy (PRIV)

**PRIV-01** · MUST · Telemetry and analytics are off by default and run only after explicit opt-in. Telemetry means any measurement that leaves the device: analytics, attribution, experiments, usage pings, diagnostics. Data kept only on the device and visible to the user is not telemetry.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no measurement leaves the device without opt-in; data manifest entry

**PRIV-02** · MUST · Unless the user adds them in the preview (PRIV-04), logs, crash reports, bug reports and diagnostic bundles contain no secrets the app holds and no content, titles or paths of the user's documents, such as notes, cards or recordings.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: redaction of content, titles and paths in logs and bundles

**PRIV-03** · MUST · Apps contact only servers the user chose. A chosen server means the user turned on the feature or started the action, and the host is named in the UI and in the privacy notice. Nothing is contacted because the app launched. On-demand downloads (dictionaries, models, fonts, the plugin directory) follow the same rule, and lookups send the minimum, not library contents.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: every host in the data manifest with its triggering action; nothing on launch

**PRIV-06** · MUST · Every privacy-affecting setting ships at its most protective value. Sharing, sync, public profiles and diagnostics stay off until the user turns them on, and no update switches on a new data flow.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new settings default to their protective value; no data flow enabled by an update

### Accessibility (A11Y)

**A11Y-01** · MUST · Every control exposes a role, a name and a state to screen readers. Icon-only controls carry an accessible name and a tooltip (UX-23); a shortened label exposes its full text as the accessible name; a disabled control exposes why it is disabled; no label repeats within a window.\
*Verified by:* CI: accessibility-tree snapshot of each window in the demo evidence; Review checklist: new controls named in the snapshot; no duplicate labels

**A11Y-02** · MUST · Every action works from the keyboard, with visible focus and documented shortcuts. Focus looks different from selection, and focus returns to its origin when a dialog closes.\
*Verified by:* CI: keyboard-only end-to-end tests, focus return after dialogs included, with focus and selection shown in the demo evidence; Review checklist: shortcuts documented

### Internationalization (I18N)

**I18N-02** · MUST · Dates, numbers, plurals, units and sorting use ICU4X with the user's locale.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: formatting through ICU4X only

### Interface (UX)

**UX-02** · MUST · Every app is built from the suite's component library and bundled fonts, so it looks the same on every platform. New patterns are class-2 decisions, may incubate in one app with Experimental status (UX-20), and are promoted when a second app needs them.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: library components only; new patterns listed as class-2 decisions; incubating patterns marked Experimental

**UX-04** · MUST · Defaults suit beginners; advanced features are disclosed progressively but always findable through search.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: new features reachable from search and the command palette (UX-11); new defaults listed as class-2 decisions

**UX-05** · MUST · Apps never use dark patterns, such as streaks that punish missed days, fake urgency, nagging or hidden cancelation.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no dark patterns

**UX-06** · MUST · Terminology follows the shared glossary in every app and language (I18N-10).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: glossary terms; Weblate consistency check (I18N-10)

**UX-07** · MUST · Error messages say what happened and what to do next, in plain language (UX-15, UX-26).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: errors name the cause and the action

**UX-21** · MUST · The interface never blocks: long work runs in the background with progress and instant cancel, and no dialog asks for input before an action that has a sensible default.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: long operations cancellable; no pre-action dialogs

**UX-25** · MUST · Apps carry no third-party advertising and never promote cryptocurrencies or related services.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no ads or cryptocurrency promotion

### Brand (BRAND)

**BRAND-05** · SHOULD · App hues are registered with at least 30° spacing and kept clear of the error, warning and success hues; every new hue is a class-2 decision, shown rendered next to the registered hues in the demo evidence, not only computed.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: hue registry entry and spacing; new hue listed as a class-2 decision; rendered hues in the demo evidence

### Performance (PERF)

**PERF-03** · MUST · Data already on the device shows without waiting for the network: no spinners for local data.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: local reads never await the network

### Platforms, distribution and updates (PLAT)

**PLAT-02** · MUST · Linux is Tier 1 for every app, and each app is at its best on Linux.\
*Verified by:* Release checklist: Linux build verified first

### Code quality and testing (QA)

**QA-02** · MUST · Libraries return typed errors and never panic on bad input; apps never crash on a recoverable error.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: error types, no panics on input

**QA-04** · MUST · Logging uses `tracing`, with structured, local, rotating logs.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: `tracing` only, rotation configured

**QA-05** · SHOULD · Public crate APIs follow the Rust API Guidelines.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: API guidelines checklist

**QA-09** · MUST · New functionality ships with tests, and every bug fix adds a test that fails without it, in the same pull request, unless the pull request explains why it cannot. While the default branch fails CI, only changes that fix it merge.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: tests in the same PR, or a stated reason

### Documentation (DOC)

**DOC-04** · MUST · ADRs live in `docs/decisions/DR-NNNN-title.md`, numbered sequentially and never reused, and follow `docs/decisions/TEMPLATE.md`: what approving it means, the context with the decision's origin and the kind of evidence behind it, at most three options with their reversibility, the recommendation, and the rollout and undo plan. An ADR fits on one screen. Status is proposed, accepted or superseded by DR-NNNN; when a later ADR supersedes only some of its decisions, the status names them, such as "row 4 superseded by DR-0009". A proposal that isn't accepted is withdrawn rather than kept. An accepted ADR is never rewritten except to change its status. Deviation ADRs carry machine-readable front matter (DOC-06).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: template, number, status, evidence line

**DOC-12** · SHOULD · Work spanning several pull requests starts from one intent whose plan sets out the shared design and lists the pull requests, and each pull request links that intent; the plan's open questions follow the dilemma protocol.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: intent linked for multi-PR work; its plan covers the pull request

**DOC-13** · MUST · Agent instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) only summarize human-facing docs; no rule or process exists only there.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: agent files cite the human-facing source

### Repository and CI (CI)

**CI-14** · SHOULD · A merged change that breaks the default branch or a release is reverted first, then re-landed with a regression test. Its author and reviewer are notified.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: revert PR links the regression test

### Code review (REV)

**REV-01** · MUST · A reviewer approves a change once it does what its intent and plan, or an outside contributor's linked issue, say, clearly improves the codebase and meets every applicable MUST in this document. Perfection is not a merge criterion; further polish is reported as an advisory finding for a follow-up issue.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: approval states what improved; follow-ups reported as advisory findings

**REV-02** · SHOULD · Reviews follow an order: is the PR valid and true to its intent or linked issue, does the approach fit, does it work, then the code itself. Every review ends with a summary of what was checked and what couldn't be. Each finding is marked blocking or advisory, and only blocking findings block a merge. Reviewers never block on personal preference or on style these conventions don't set, and never widen a PR's scope. Details: the review rubric (CI-03).\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: summary present; each finding marked blocking or advisory

**REV-04** · MUST · Review disagreements, design disputes included, are settled by data first, then by this document, then by the founder in a decision pull request. The decision and its reason are recorded on the PR.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: decision recorded on the PR, with its decision pull request linked

### Governance and contribution (GOV)

**GOV-02** · MUST · The author of a change owns its intent, specification, tests and consequences, and can explain what it does and why, whether or not AI wrote the code; for an agent's change, the author is the person who directed it. Every change gets the independent AI review (CI-03), line by line on risk-tier paths, on top of the automated gates every change passes (CI-02). Each project lists its risk-tier paths in its `project.toml`, which the review tooling reads.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: linked intent or issue; risk-tier paths read from `project.toml` and reviewed line by line

**GOV-03** · MUST · AI assistance is disclosed. Every commit in which AI produced anything beyond single-line completion carries the `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming the model, as emitted by the tooling, and the squash commit keeps every such trailer from the branch. The pull request says how AI was used, what it produced, the human creative input (the intent, design, selection, editing), and what verified it, such as the checks, the independent AI review (CI-03) and any human check. Disclosure covers code, docs, RFCs, ADRs, issues and review comments.\
*Verified by:* CI: squash commit carries the branch's trailers; Review checklist: disclosure block present

**GOV-06** · MUST · The code of conduct is [Contributor Covenant 3.0](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/3/0/code_of_conduct/), with a private reporting address; GOV-21 completes its reporting section before the project opens to outside contributions. Its scope covers the forge, chat, forum and events; app names, descriptions, screenshots and bundled content; and content an AI agent posts under a person's name.\
*Verified by:* CI: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md from the template; Review checklist

**GOV-17** · MUST · AI-created code meets a higher test bar: every edge case the author or reviewer can name is tested, and no untested path merges. Generated code that isn't an extension or refactor of existing project code gets a provenance check (LEGAL-11) before merging.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: edge cases listed and tested; coverage and missed-mutant results on the PR where the checks report them

**GOV-25** · SHOULD · The organization doesn't ship model-generated functional media, such as UI icons or placeholder images. Any that ships is revised by a human, disclosed per file in REUSE metadata and license-checked.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: provenance, disclosure and license check per file

**GOV-26** · MUST · Procedural media, generated by a reviewable algorithm whose parameters are in the repository, is not model-generated media, whoever wrote the code. Its code is reviewed like any other (GOV-02, GOV-17), and its output is checked not to reproduce another work. Coordinates or samples a model writes directly, such as SVG path data, count as model-generated media.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: generator in the repository; output provenance check

### Licensing and compliance (LEGAL)

**LEGAL-08** · MUST · Default licenses unless an ADR says otherwise (LEGAL-01): user documentation, art, icons and media CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-SA 4.0, one chosen by ADR; CC0-1.0 for small reusable assets, generated files and trivial data; translations take their source file's license; build and CI scripts take the code license; third-party data keeps its license. NonCommercial or NoDerivatives terms appear nowhere. Code licenses follow LEGAL-01.\
*Verified by:* `reuse lint` with the allowed-license list

**LEGAL-09** · MUST · No AI system is named as author or co-author in copyright notices, AUTHORS files or copyright registrations. Commit trailers (GOV-03) are not author fields.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: no AI in notices or AUTHORS

**LEGAL-11** · MUST · Code copied from elsewhere, including AI output that reproduces it, keeps its license and attribution and is compatible with the target artifact. Contributors never copy from, or consult, source-available or proprietary implementations of formats the suite imports; interoperability is built from public specifications and sample files.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: provenance of new code (GOV-17)

**LEGAL-14** · MUST · Every asset is committed in, or next to, its preferred modifiable form (SVG or design source for icons and logos, token sources for generated styles), with instructions to regenerate it. Binary assets (fonts, images, test fixtures) live in a declared directory with provenance notes.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: source form and provenance for every new asset

### Lifecycle and continuity (LIFE)

**LIFE-07** · MUST · The organization publishes the list of its official repositories, on kreqo.org and in the template.\
*Verified by:* CI: repository list generated and published

### Business model and stewardship (BIZ)

**BIZ-03** · MUST · Nothing is ever taken from the open apps. A released feature is never moved to a paid tier, held back by a delay, time-limited or artificially capped, such as by limits on the amount of user content, devices or sync size. The open apps download and run with no email, account or sign-in, and benchmarking is allowed.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist; Release checklist: feature list diff against the last release

### AI features in the apps (AIF)

**AIF-01** · MUST · AI features are optional, off by default and run on the device by default. Models are downloaded only at the user's request, from a named source with checksum and license shown, and are declared in the data manifest. Only models whose license and training-data provenance are documented and compatible are used.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: manifest entry; CI: default settings test

**AIF-02** · MUST · Sending user content to a remote model needs a per-feature opt-in that names the provider and what is sent. Users choose the provider, including a local runtime or their own endpoint, and nothing goes to a default third party.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: consent screen reviewed; data manifest entry

**AIF-03** · MUST · User content is never used to train or fine-tune models, by Kreqo or by any integrated provider, and never read by humans for model evaluation; integrations use only providers that contractually exclude training.\
*Verified by:* Review checklist: provider terms on file for each integration
